# Orient in the architecture before changing its shape

The architecture of Sarah is specified in this repository as a knowledge
graph, generated from Ergane. It is not documentation written after the
fact: it is the record the architects work in, and it is regenerated
whenever they change it.

## Read in this order

1. **The architecture description documents**, the markdown files in
   `architecture/` beside `README.md`. The prose account of what this
   system is for and how it hangs together.
   - `architecture/objectives-and-business-case.md`
   - `architecture/architecture-description.md`
   - `architecture/requirements-specification.md`
   - `architecture/decision-log.md`
2. **`architecture/graph.json`** — the backbone. `nodeTypes` says what
   kinds of thing exist, `nodes` lists every artifact with the path to
   its data and when it last changed, and `edges` carries the typed
   relationships: requirement to decision, decision to model element,
   model element to capability.
3. **`architecture/entities/<type>/INDEX.md`** — one line per artifact of
   a type. Navigate from here; open an individual `.codl.json` only when
   you need that artifact's detail.
4. **`architecture/definitions/<type>.codl-def.json`** — what a field
   MEANS, what values it may take, and which other types it may legally
   link to. Read this before you interpret a field you have not seen.
5. **`architecture/models/*.calm.json`** — the architecture models, in
   FINOS CALM. Each has a `*.links.json` beside it mapping elements of
   the model to the decisions and requirements that govern them.

A card may hold more than one model, and each is its own file, named for
the field it came from. A model in another notation is `.model.json`
rather than `.calm.json`, and its `.links.json` says which notation.

Where a document embeds a model, this bundle names the model and links to
its data rather than drawing it — diagrams are not published yet. The model
file is the record; position and layout are deliberately not part of it.

## What to do with what you find

- The specification is **authoritative**. Where the code and the
  specification disagree, that is a finding to report — see the
  architecture drift skill — not a licence to change the specification to
  match the code.
- `architecture/definitions/` is **read-only**. It is the professional
  body's ontology (IASA BTABoK), not this project's.
- Never hand-edit anything under `architecture/`, nor the generated
  documents in the repository root. They are regenerated on the next
  publish and your edit is lost. To change the record, use the
  architecture change proposal skill.
- Ergane owns `architecture/` plus exactly the paths listed under
  `ownership.machineOwnedPaths` in `architecture/manifest.json`.
  Everything else in this repository is yours and is never touched by a
  publish.
- Position and layout are deliberately excluded. Where a box sits on a
  board is not part of the meaning.
- To build a ticket the architecture describes, use the architecture
  implementation skill.
